title: Plugin-driven micro-bench harness; deprecate legacy gRPC stubs
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Summary:
Refactor the existing performance and evaluation harness into a plugin-driven micro-benchmarking scaffold and remove the legacy generated gRPC Python stubs to simplify onboarding, reduce image size, and make local iteration faster. The new scaffold (micro-bench mode) should let engineers run small, deterministic workloads locally or in CI (< 10m for smoke runs) while preserving the full-scale regression suite used for production regression runs.

Goals:
- Introduce a plugin interface for data sources, runners, and metric collectors so new workloads (embedding, reranking, chat) can be added without changing core harness code.
- Add a "micro-bench" execution mode (lightweight, deterministic, fast-seed) for quick CI feedback and local profiling.
- Deprecate the legacy grpcio-tools generated stubs and move to an async-first, typed client layer (betterproto or hand-written async HTTP adapters) to remove C-extension build complexity from CI and packaging.
- Upgrade critical dependencies (protobuf >= 4.21, numpy >= 1.26, torch >= 2.1) and remove or relax several pinned transitive deps that cause frequent conflicts in downstream projects.
- Add deterministic seeding and an optional HTTP/SDK replay fixture mechanism (VCR-style) for reproducible perf comparisons.

Scope (in-scope):
- New plugin interface and reference adapters for: synthetic load generator, synthetic KV-cached generation, and the existing JSON-line scenario runner.
- Micro-bench mode implementation and CI workflow for fast smoke checks.
- Migration layer that keeps the old harness available behind a feature flag until adapters are migrated.
- Dependency bumps listed above and small code changes to accommodate new API surfaces.

Out of scope:
- Full rewrite of every existing runner/adapter. We'll migrate adapters incrementally.
- Any runtime-level kernel optimizations (those belong in runtime team epics) — this is harness-level work.

Acceptance criteria:
- All existing perf regression scenarios can run under the new harness and produce matching metric names and tags.
- Micro-bench CI smoke job completes end-to-end under 10 minutes on the CI agent image.
- Base Docker image size for perf-harness drops by at least 40MB by removing grpcio C-extensions.
- Dependency upgrades do not cause failing downstream projects (run subset consumer matrix).
- Documentation page and migration guide published (Confluence) and referenced in the console release notes.

Migration plan / rollout:
1) Implement plugin interface and micro-bench mode behind a feature flag.
2) Ship reference adapters and run both harness versions in parallel in perf CI for 2 weeks to compare outputs.
3) Gradually port critical adapters (KV, streaming, embedding) and deprecate old gRPC stubs after no regressions are observed for one cycle.
4) Flip feature flag and remove legacy code in a follow-up cleanup ticket.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Removing gRPC generated stubs simplifies packaging but may require shims for internal services that expect bi-directional streaming; plan to provide a lightweight shim adapter for long-lived streaming tests.
- Dependency bumps could reveal subtle numerical differences in model code paths; we will capture baseline outputs and use the deterministic replay to detect meaningful deltas.
- Short micro-bench runs may mask concurrency-related regressions only visible in full-scale runs — keep the full regression suite in nightly runs.

Diagnostics / Observability:
- New harness must emit the same metric labels used by perf dashboards (job, scenario, model, seed).
- Add a quick health dashboard for micro-bench CI jobs with pass/fail, median latency, and token/sec trends. Link: https://grafana.internal.redwood.ai/d/bench/micro-bench-overview

Artifacts / Links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Plugin+Perf+Harness
- Spike notebook & results: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-example-spike
- Active PR (work-in-progress): https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-harness/pull/412
- Baseline perf dashboard: https://grafana.internal.redwood.ai/d/bench/regen-suite

Next steps:
- Complete adapter interface review with runtime and infra teams (scheduled 2025-11-18).
- Land the initial plugin scaffolding and micro-bench runner (PR #412) and get a green CI matrix for a small consumer subset.
- Open follow-ups for shims and final grpc stub removal after metrics validation.
